text:
Arshdeep Bains grew up in Surrey, went undrafted, scored 112 points in his last WHL season, and worked his way through Abbotsford to a job with his hometown-region Canucks. With Filip Chytil out, his minutes have climbed to about 13 a night, up from around 10.

The production is modest, three points in 14 games, and it has been a learning stretch. Daniel Wagner flagged rough defending on Mattias Ekholm's goal Saturday, leaving him open for a one-timer. The five-on-five numbers are better than that moment suggests: Vancouver has been about four points of expected goal share better with him on the ice than without him, at 44%.

He isn't fast, with NHL Edge putting his top speed in the bottom 15% of the league, so his game has to be about positioning and puck support. Evolving-Hockey had too little of him last season to say much. Our range says 4 to 11 goals over a full season. On a team in a skid, every depth forward is auditioning, and Bains has the advantage of being a player the Canucks developed themselves.
headline: Bains gets more minutes
